- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, failing to capture the true peak or subsequent mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices are trending upward.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price declines — often underestimates a falling trend until it’s already passed.
- Model shows strong bias toward higher prices in the middle of the forecast horizon, especially when historical mean is rising.
- Model fails to capture the “mean reversion” effect after sustained upward trends — tends to keep prices high longer than they should.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike too early and too high, then fails to adjust downward as market stabilizes.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or supply shocks in the final 10 days — often misses the true peak or trough in the last 5–7 days.
